show.title: The Birdcage
show.headline: Robin Williams and Nathan Lane try to play it straight

event.title: <show-title>The Birdcage</show-title>
event.headline: Williams & Lane burst open THE BIRDCAGE in this flamboyant farcical adaptation
event.description:
"My mother always said, 'Live on Fisher Island, get buried in Palm Beach. That way, you'll have the best of Florida.'"

Progress is not a straight line. I mean, I’m not sure it’s a line at all. It seems far more abstract and subjective. Like, listen: in 1996, when THE BIRDCAGE was first released, the idea of a mainstream comedy film with two gay leads (and many more openly queer characters) was controversial. I guess, unfortunately…it still is.

Based on the French farce film LA CAGE AUX FOLLES from 1978, Mike Nichols and Elaine May’s adaptation shifts the action from a drag club in the French Riviera to a drag club in South Beach, Florida…the American Riviera. When Armand Goldman (Robin Williams) learns that his son Val (Dan Futterman) is engaged to the daughter of conservative couple Senator Kevin Keeley (Gene Hackman) and Louise Keeley (Dianne Wiest), he’s put into an impossible situation. Pushed by Val to “straighten” out his life in preparation for meeting his fiancée Barbara’s (Calista Flockhart) parents, Armand struggles to manage his life partner Albert (Nathan Lane) with some dubious assistance from their housemaid Agador (Hank Azaria) and Val’s birth mother Katharine (Christine Brianski). Shenanigans ensue: there’s drag, Fosse, pierced toast, beckoning schmecken, and of course DRAG! WHEW! Grounded by hilarious and deeply heartfelt performances from Williams and Lane, THE BIRDCAGE is an incredible (if sometimes problematic) comedy helmed by the iconic duo of Nichols and May. Immensely quotable and uncomfortably relevant 30 years after its release, THE BIRDCAGE is a classic, and we’re so excited to screen it as part of Queer Film Theory 101!

show.title: Daughters of Darkness
show.headline: They are waiting for you...they thrive on blood!

event.title: <show-title>Daughters of Darkness</show-title>
event.headline: Delphine Seyrig dazzles in this 1970s erotic lesbian vampire cult classic
event.description:
"I'm just an outmoded character, nothing more. You know, the beautiful stranger, slightly sad, slightly… mysterious… that haunts one place after another."

In the early 1970s, hardboiled crime films were all the rage: CHINATOWN, THE GODFATHER, THE FRENCH CONNECTION dominated the cineplex across the country. But simultaneously, there was another genre on the rise: the erotic lesbian vampire film. From THE VAMPIRE LOVERS to SHIVER OF THE VAMPIRES to VAMPYRES (which you know is queer because of its unconventional spelling), the era was riddled with attempts to cash in on the new lezzie blood-sucking craze. A standout from the red deluge of immortal sapphic stories was DAUGHTERS OF DARKNESS, a French, Belgian, and German collaboration helmed by Harry Kümel. When chaotic newlywed couple Valerie (Danielle Ouimet) and Stefan (John Karlen) arrive at a grand hotel on the Ostend seafront during the off-season, they initially seem to be the only guests in residence. That is, until the glamorous and preternaturally youthful Hungarian countess Elizabeth Báthory (Delphine Seyrig) arrives with her icy secretary Ilona (Andrea Rau). The Countess quickly becomes fixated on Valerie, and the dubious honeymoon is thrown into bizarre and erotic disarray.

Featuring an incredible and funky score by François de Roubaix and stunning decadent garments, DAUGHTERS OF DARKNESS is a vibe, and it’s so queeeeer. Decadent, alluring, dreamy, and strange, we can’t wait to watch this gorgeous film with you on the big screen as part of Queer Film Theory 10. Come, glamorous darlings, haunt us with your startling visage.

show.title: A Tale of Two Sisters
show.headline: Every family has its dark secrets

event.title: <show-title>A Tale of Two Sisters</show-title>
event.headline: Sad Girl Cinema Club gets spooky with Kim Jee-woon’s top tier twisted tale
event.description:
A TALE OF TWO SISTERS begins with Su-mi’s (Im Soo-jung) return home from her time away at a mental institution, and her homecoming is less than ideal. Her heavily medicated stepmother Eun-joo (Yum Jung-ah) rules the house, erratic and violent, she often terrified her younger sister Su-yeon (Moon Geun-young). However, their stepmother is not the only one wreaking havoc in their home: the ghost of their mother also haunts them in the evenings, fragmenting the barrier between what is real and what is psychosis.

Korean New Wave spearhead Kim Jee-woon’s diabolical fairy tale is filled with twists and turns. A TALE OF TWO SISTERS is an achingly haunted tale of sisterhood, evil stepmothers, and deadbeat dads. A luscious slow burn, the film to this day remains one of the most affecting Korean horror films of all time.

What is girlhood without a little bit of insanity?

event.title: <show-title>Ginger Snaps</show-title>
event.headline: The ultimate feminist werewolf parable
event.description: One of the dumbest prejudices perpetuated by the world is that menstrual cycles turn women into monsters. That conceit is what makes GINGER SNAPS so powerful. The Fitzgerald sisters (Katharine Isabelle and Emily Perkins) are death-obsessed high school goths who create violent art projects while battling the popular kids. But everything changes when someone’s period – and a werewolf – enters the picture. Written by Karen Walton as a feminist werewolf parable, GINGER SNAPS is an essential Y2K ripper that has lost none of its freshness, relevance, or bite over the past two decades.

Q: Are we not men?
A: WE ARE MANOS!

Mike (Harold P. Warren) and Maggie (Diane Mahree) are on a road trip with their daughter and family dog. But they take a wrong turn and wind up at a lodge inhabited by a polygamous pagan cult! The family finds themselves in the middle of a power struggle between caretaker Torgo (John Reynolds), cult leader The Master (Tom Neyman), and two warring factions of the Master’s wives. The sole directorial effort of Texas fertilizer salesman Warren, MANOS: THE HANDS OF FATE is an absurdist masterpiece. Prepare to exit the planet.

event.title: <show-title>Littermates</show-title> <event-type-title>Advance Screening</event-type-title>
event.headline: Catch the latest Alamo Exclusives film early
event.description:
At Chester’s cottage, good behavior earns karaoke. Getting answers is a little more complicated.

After a mysterious apocalyptic(ish) attack leaves them bloodied, disoriented, and unable to speak, Liam (Joey Bader) and Mel (Kaylee McGregor) take refuge in the English countryside. Their oddball host, Chester (Oliver Woolf), feeds them, helps them recover, and introduces a system of rewards: behave yourself, earn “nifties,” cash them in for hot-tub time and dance parties.

Beyond the cottage, things are less nifty. But within it, a makeshift family is taking shape. While Liam embraces their new life, Mel grows increasingly curious about the world Chester insists is too dangerous to enter…

In their feature debut, directors Scott Tinkham and Michael Woloson mix deadpan comedy, sibling rivalry, and creeping unease in a coming-of-age story about people who have to grow up all over again. Winner of the Special Jury Prize at the 2026 Manchester Film Festival and the Narrative Feature Audience Award at Dances With Films LA 2026, this has the sort of sensibilities that fans of Yorgos Lanthimos and Ben Wheatley will adore… and it’s a natural fit as an Alamo Exclusive.

event.title: <show-title>Faust (1926)</show-title> <event-type-title>w/ Invincible Czars</event-type-title>
event.headline: Celebrating 100 years of Murnau's enduring masterwork.
event.description:
In 2026, The Invincible Czars celebrate 100 years of the silent masterpiece Faust (1926, FW Murnau) by performing their tastefully modern soundtrack live with the movie at theatres in the US and Canada. Their brand new electrifying score marries new and old elements of classical music, bossa nova and even a touch of heavy metal to bring the movie to life for contemporary audiences and incorporates a mix of instruments like flute, violin and electric guitar.

The Invincible Czars’s score for Faust is mostly original material inspired by film score composers like Bernard Herrman and John Williams peppered with and cinematic metal a la Fantomas and even a little Marcos Valle-esque bossa nova. The band keeps their tradition of incorporating music from Russian classical composers, revisiting their renditions of Mussorgsy’s Pictures at an Exhibition and A Night on Bald Mountain in particular for this soundtrack. Five players perform the score live on violin, electric guitar, clarinet, bass clarinet, flute, glockenspiel, keyboard and drums.

show.title: Nosferatu (1922)
show.headline: The silent classic based on the story of Dracula

event.title: <show-title>Nosferatu (1922)</show-title> <event-type-title>with the Invincible Czars</event-type-title>
event.headline: A haunting live score for F.W. Murnau's silent classic
event.description:
Alamo Drafthouse is proud to present the return of an annual Halloween tradition – Invincible Czars’ live score for NOSFERATU. Since 2006, the Austin-based band has been performing well-crafted and critically-acclaimed original silent film scores for THE CABINET OF DR. CALIGARI, Lon Chaney’s THE PHANTOM OF THE OPERA, John Barrymore’s DR. JEKYLL & MR. HYDE, Lillian Gish’s THE WIND, and so many others.

The Invincible Czars have updated their soundtrack for NOSFERATU in preparation to release a recording for the film’s centennial in 2022. This will be the debut of the updated score incorporating violin, organ, flute, bass clarinet, drums, percussion, vocals, music box, synthesizers, electric guitar, piano, and many sound effects performed live and in-theater by only five performers. Drawing from the realm of classical music, Invincible Czars’ score incorporates original music inspired by Bela Bartok’s Roumanian Folk Dances as a nod to the fictional Count Orlok’s home turf.

Directed by F.W. Murnau and starring the terrifying Max Schreck, NOSFERATU is one of the most revered films in the history of cinema, and the very first – and possibly best – adaptation of Bram Stoker’s Dracula. The film would nearly be erased from the history books after the estate of Bram Stoker sued the filmmakers for copyright infringement, and nearly all the prints of the movie were destroyed. Only a few survived, and this performance features the most complete existing version.

show.headline: The most amazing story ever screened

event.title: <show-title>The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari</show-title> <event-type-title>w/ Invincible Czars</event-type-title>
event.headline: The critically acclaimed score performed live
event.description:
This Halloween season, The Invincible Czars return to Alamo Drafthouse Cinema locations across the country with their nightmarish-ly fun soundtrack to the world’s first feature-length horror film, F.W. Murnau's THE CABINET OF DR. CALIGARI (1920). With an immersive combined live soundtrack experience that transports audiences back 100+ years, the age-old tale is accompanied by a chilling, tastefully-modern score featuring an impressive blend of traditional acoustic and present-day electric instruments.

The band will also perform their critically acclaimed soundtrack for NOSFERATU at select locations.

THE CABINET OF DR. CALIGARI is essential cinema, inspiring numerous present-day filmmakers with its strikingly modern visuals. Its craggy edges, disjointed backgrounds, and heavy makeup have earned this dark fairy tale a reputation as the quintessential German Expressionist film. Its twist ending is also considered the first in cinematic history (and something Rod Sterling’s The Twilight Zone capitalized upon in the 1960s).

The live accompaniment experience marries the old-world charm of silent film with a contemporary electricity, engaging multi-generational audiences. “We strive to create soundtracks that give modern-day audiences a context to appreciate these 100-year-old movies,” said Josh Robins, Invincible Czars founder and bandleader. The group draws upon influences from more modern film composers including Bear McCreary, Angelo Badalmenti, David Buckley, Bernard Herrmann, and Danny Elfman

Fans, theaters, and media have consistently praised The Invincible Czars’ carefully crafted soundtracks for enhancing movie-goers’ experience. The band has performed for over a decade at hundreds of theaters and art houses across the US and Canada, delighting audiences with an array of sonic twists and turns. The varied compositions and instrumentation adapt individually to each film the Czars score, capturing each thrilling moment and keeping audiences engaged scene by scene.

Their score is performed by a five-member touring ensemble using violin, flute, bass clarinet, oboe, electric guitar, bass guitar, piano, organ, glockenspiel, music box, drums, percussion, samples, and loops. From delicate passages of longing and love to menacing motifs of dissonant horror and pain, each instrument plays a critical role in establishing character themes and creating an aural dreamscape for the film.

ABOUT THE FILM

THE CABINET OF DR. CALIGARI tells the story of a group of friends who encounter the mysterious Dr. Caligari and his scary, sleepwalking sidekick Cesare at a carnival. When a series of murders brings the town to its knees, Franzis sets out to prove Caligari is responsible…but is he?

ABOUT THE BAND

The Invincible Czars began making adventurous rock music in Austin clubs in 2003, but they quickly branched into the art world with their wide scope of styles, cinematic flare, mix of modern and classical instruments, and their complicated relationship with heavy metal.

Though they continue to take on a variety of projects, including their Austin-tacious re-imagining of Tchaikovsky‘s Nutcracker Suite, The Invincible Czars are probably best known for their silent film soundtracks which they perform live at cinemas, colleges, and performing arts spaces all over the US and Canada.

They began accompanying silent films at the original Alamo Drafthouse in Austin in 2006 with AELITA, QUEEN OF MARS (1924). They continued adding titles to their catalog year after year and expanding their performance region slowly until they were touring the entire US by 2016. Many arthouse cinemas and film festivals call The Invincible Czars one of the best in the nation for silent film accompaniment. “Thank you for making this movie actually scary,” is heard at least once at every show.

The band operates as a collective with a few core members and a rotating cast of additional members on any given project or tour. They sound different from season to season and year to year. The touring ensemble for 2023 is:

Phil Davidson – violin, keyboards, percussion
Skunk Manhattan – piano, keyboards, bass
Josh Robins – guitar, bass, samples, percussion
Louis Landry – drums, percussion, keyboards
Hampton Rattan – winds, keys

event.title: <show-title>House of 1000 Corpses</show-title>
event.headline: Rob Zombie’s Halloween-set slasher in 35mm.
event.description:
This is the idealization of a horror movie that you’d stumble upon at 2am while channel surfing on acid in 1984. A valentine to every aesthetic touchpoint that Rob Zombie loved circa Y2K—including THE TEXAS CHAIN SAW MASSACRE, Alice Cooper, and PULP FICTION—HOUSE OF 1000 CORPSES is a Halloween-set slasher that’s off the rails in the best way possible. This hypercolored nightmare was filmed on a combination of 16mm, 35mm, Super 8, and VHS. That collage-like approach is perfectly replicated by the tone, which jumps from cartoonish camp to grotesque violence at the drop of a machete.

Screening an archival 35mm print courtesy of the American Genre Film Archive.

event.headline: The Y2K analog experiment from Takashi Shimizu.
event.description:
Screening in Japanese with English subtitles.

This month, Terror Tuesday presents THIS HOUSE IS HAUNTED—four expeditions to our favorite haunted dwellings.

Welcome to the J-horror movie that fueled a million night terrors. Before JU-ON: THE GRUDGE, there was JU-ON: THE CURSE—the Y2K analog horror experiment that was written and directed by JU-ON franchise creator Takashi Shimizu under the guidance of Kiyoshi Kurosawa (PULSE). The story follows the present-day tenants of a cursed home as they uncover the secrets of Kayako, a vengeful ghost who would soon become one of Japan’s biggest horror icons. Filmed on lo-fi video cameras and never screened in U.S. theaters, JU-ON: THE CURSE is a minimalist exploration of liminal dread that doubles as a cozy, late-summer campfire tale.

show.headline: Jamie Blanks' post-SCREAM slasher

event.title: <show-title>Urban Legend</show-title>
event.headline: Jamie Blanks' slasher film gives us a killer reveal to end all killer reveals
event.description: In the wake of SCREAM's success in 1996, Hollywood did what Hollywood does best: greenlit a bunch of copycats to capitalize on a successful film's...success. In terms of SCREAM, that meant that we were seeing a lot of relatively tame (at least when compared to their '80s counterparts) slasher films featuring up-and-coming stars from the WB Network. What is interesting about this wave of post-SCREAM slashers is that they're less copycats of SCREAM (a self-referential, meta exercise in horror fandom), and more so '90s versions of the '80s slashers that SCREAM was commenting on. One such example is Jamie Blanks' URBAN LEGEND, a wildly fun film with a fantastic gimmick (the killer themes all of his/her/their kills after well-known urban legends). While the film doesn't stray too far outside the lines of the slasher playbook, it's memorable for its creative murder set pieces and one truly exceptional killer reveal that we won't spoil here. Blanks would try to replicate his success to lesser results with 2001's VALENTINE, but URBAN LEGEND remains his magnum opus. (Trace Thurman)

event.headline: ... takes HOLLYWOOD by the throat and STRANGLES it!
event.description:
Edgar Allan (Rufus B. Seder) is an aspiring screenwriter who has just come to Hollywood to make it in the movies... only to wind up working as the janitor at a fleabag apartment complex run by the greasy ex-boxer Martin (George Kuchar) instead. When Edgar begins channeling his frustrations with his kooky neighbors into fodder for his latest screenplay, the vivid murder scenes he writes begin to happen for real. As the bodies begin to pile up and the line between reality and fiction become increasingly blurred, Edgar, who is convinced that the only way to be a real writer is to suffer, is slowly driven mad.

Inventively produced using a host of early cinematic techniques and featuring a memorable performance by underground film legend George Kuchar, Rufus Butler Seder's Screamplay is a singularly charming tribute to Old Hollywood and a marvel of low-budget but high-concept filmmaking.

DCP courtesy of Muscle Distribution

The Duke of Norwich is mad as a hatter! To prove it, he tortures and murders anyone who might pose a threat to his coveted throne. This includes the Duke’s gay hunchback lover, a one-eyed witch, and dirt-eating peasants. In addition to Milligan’s patented blend of caustic bickering, no-fi gore, and elegant costumes, this movie also includes the best line of dialogue that the deranged filmmaker ever wrote: “I’m trisexual — I’ll try anything for pleasure!” (AGFA)

marketStrings.value: The personal closed captioning device displays feature film dialogue and other audio in the form of English-language text for individuals who are deaf or hard of hearing.

The descriptive audio headset provides individuals who are blind or have low vision with an English-language narration of the details of the feature presentation that can't be understood by the soundtrack alone.

Upon request at the box office, we provide assistive listening headsets with amplified audio for those individuals who are hard of hearing. For guests who prefer to use their own hearing aids, neck loops, or cochlear implants, our assistive listening headsets have a 3.5mm headphone jack to connect to those devices.

In order to ensure the highest quality experience for all guests, you may not enter a movie after it has started. We’d love to see you up to 30 minutes early. Running late? No worries, we will happily exchange your ticket for a different showtime or a raincheck to a future show.

formats.title: HDR by Barco
formats.headline: Next-level technology that artfully directs light & unlocks a film's potential.
formats.description: A next-level cinema technology from Barco that artfully directs light to unlock the full potential of every film. With darker darks, brighter brights, and a full spectrum of vibrant, life-like colors you can see every detail and feel every moment when you choose to experience extraordinary in HDR by Barco.
